item.description:
A series of tax cuts since President George W. Bush's 2001 legislation have helped push the national debt to US$32 trillion. AP Photo/Ron Edmonds Democrats, set to take over Congress with robust majorities, will face at least one expensive obstacle to their policy agenda: a national debt that now equals the size of the U.S. economy. Clocking in at US$32 trillion, this debt-to-GDP ratio of 100% would likely raise alarms for other countries. But it attracted relatively little attention in an election season dominated by concerns over the economy and the cost of living . Debt has grown to these levels because over the past 25 years, the federal government has been spending more than it collects in taxes . item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials say
item.description:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation. The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians. Continue reading...

item.title: John Kerry: America Must Now Follow China’s Lead on Clean Energy
item.description:
This story was originally published by The Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe—including the United States—must now follow, former US Secretary of State John Kerry has told The Guardian , as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit. As Cop31 opens—this year the climate conference is in Turkey —there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance.” Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do. item.title: Oil shock from Iran war led to drop in carbon pollution, scientists say
item.description:
Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over” . Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end. Continue reading...

item.title: Senate Advances Bipartisan Permitting Bill That Could Unleash Energy Development With Major Caveats
item.description:
On Monday evening, the Senate moved one step closer to passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) with a 73–25 procedural vote to bring the bill to the floor for the full chamber to consider. Sponsored by Sen. Shelley Moore Capito (R–W.Va.), chairwoman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, the 494-page bill would modify the federal permitting process by limiting the scope of environmental reviews and expediting the timeline for project approval. The federal permitting process has stifled development in America's energy, housing, and transportation industries for decades. The average timeline to complete an environmental impact statement—the most stringent review under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)—is over two years, according to a 2025 report by the White House Council on Environmental Quality. item.title: Jaylen Brown gives former teammate Jayson Tatum frosty greeting as Celtics beat 76ers
item.description:
The weightlessness of the early season and the ever-increasing rate of injuries can make it hard to sell a weeknight NBA game in November. There remains, however, a reliable shortcut between "box score I'll check in the morning" and "game I gotta watch live," and it is a route lined with beef. Beef was not promised in the lead up to Tuesday night's game between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers, which pit former teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum against each other for the first time since Brown was traded in the offseason, but a savory aroma was in the air.
